# Fix: `E0046` on a feature-gated `WriteTxn` impl that default-feature builds never compile

**Class:** `rust-e0046-trait-impl-missing-under-feature-gate`
**Repo:** `hermes-rs` · **broken:** `a5dcc10` · **fixed:** `7a349058bba02b202ff702489d434de46eb18416`
**Trait:** `WriteTxn` (`src/persistence/api.rs`) · **gated impl:** `TursoBackend` (`src/persistence/turso_backend.rs:512`)
**Gate command:** `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

## 1. Symptom

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --workspace` | **GREEN** (exit 0, all targets `ok`, new regression tests pass) |
| `cargo build --workspace --all-features` | **RED** (exit 101) — `error[E0046]: not all trait items implemented, missing: append_messages_batch --> src/persistence/turso_backend.rs:512` |

The same `--all-features` failure hit the CI lint/build leg on every push.

## 2. Root cause

`WriteTxn` has multiple impls; one is compiled only under the opt-in `turso` feature:

```toml
[features]
turso = ["dep:turso", "dep:tokio"]
```
```rust
#[cfg(feature = "turso")]
pub mod turso_backend;
```

`turso` is **not** in the default feature set, so a plain `cargo test --workspace` never parses/types-checks `turso_backend.rs` — `cfg`-stripped modules are removed *before* name resolution and trait checking. When a new **required** method `append_messages_batch` was added to `WriteTxn`, only `SqliteWriteTxn` was updated. The missing method on `TursoBackend` is invisible under default features and only `E0046` fires under `--all-features`.

**Key insight:** default-feature compilation is not a subset check over gated code paths. Green default + red `--all-features` is the signature of this class.

> Not to be confused with Cargo **feature unification** (E0599 / `serialize_struct` not found). That is about a dependency's features leaking across members (`resolver = "2"`); this is a *local* `impl` being `cfg`-stripped from the compilation unit.

## 3. Exact fix

### 3.1 Enumerate impls by source, not compiler output

```bash
grep -rn "impl WriteTxn for" src/
grep -rn "cfg(feature" src/persistence/          # which impls can be stripped
```
```
src/persistence/stock_sqlite.rs:  impl WriteTxn for SqliteWriteTxn   # already fixed
src/persistence/turso_backend.rs: impl WriteTxn for TursoBackend    # MISSING -> fix
```

### 3.2 Implement the method on every impl, including the gated one

```rust
// src/persistence/turso_backend.rs (inside impl WriteTxn for TursoBackend)
fn append_messages_batch(&mut self, messages: &[NewMessage]) -> Result<()> {
    if messages.is_empty() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    // One transaction for the whole batch: all rows land or none do.
    let tx = self.conn.transaction()?;
    for message in messages {
        append_message_in_tx(&tx, message)?;
    }
    tx.commit()?;
    Ok(())
}
```

(If the backend has a native bulk-insert API, delegate to it instead.) Keep `api.rs` + `stock_sqlite.rs` as the source of truth and conform the Turso impl.

### 3.3 Format before pushing

```bash
cargo fmt --all && cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

### 3.4 Adopt the full-feature gate (prevention)

```bash
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings   # guard
cargo build  --workspace --all-features                               # minimum
```

Wire the guard into CI lint/test legs with `--all-features` everywhere so gated impls always enter the compilation unit.

## 4. Verification (in order)

| # | Command | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` | exit **0** (was 101 + E0046) |
| 2 | `cargo build --workspace --all-features` | exit **0** |
| 3 | `cargo test --workspace` | exit **0**, all targets `ok`, incl. two new regression tests |
| 4 | `cargo test --workspace --all-features` | exit **0** (exercises the real Turso impl set) |
| 5 | `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | exit **0** |
| 6 | CI after push | **3/3** legs success; pre-fix run shows Format-leg failure |

## 5. Trap to remember

- Green `cargo test --workspace` ≠ complete trait addition when an impl is `cfg`-gated.
- Green default build + red `--all-features` build is the signature of this class.
- Default and `--all-features` test runs exercise **different impl sets** — any "the repo builds" criterion must name the feature set.
- On every trait-method change: `grep -rn "impl <Trait> for" src/` cross-checked with `grep -rn "cfg(feature" src/`. Never rely on the default compiler to report missing gated impls.

---

**Note:** this environment has no `hermes-rs` checkout and no `cargo`/`rustc` installed, so I could not execute the commands here; the verification table states the results to be reproduced in the repo (and matches the fix commit's known CI outcome: 3/3 legs green, pre-fix Format leg red).

signatures.description:
SYMPTOM: `cargo test --workspace` was GREEN (exit 0, every target ok, new regression tests passing) while `cargo build --workspace --all-features` was RED with `error[E0046]: not all trait items implemented, missing: append_messages_batch --> src/persistence/turso_backend.rs:512`. The same failure surfaced on every push as a CI format/build leg failure. A developer who added a method to a shared trait and ran only the default test command genuinely believes the repo builds.

ROOT CAUSE: the crate defines a backend abstraction as a trait (`WriteTxn` in src/persistence/api.rs) with multiple implementations, and one implementation is compiled only when an OPT-IN feature is enabled:
  # Cargo.toml
  [features]
  turso = ["dep:turso", "dep:tokio"]
  // src/persistence/mod.rs
  #[cfg(feature = "turso")]
  pub mod turso_backend;
  #[cfg(feature = "turso")]
  pub use turso_backend::TursoBackend;
The `turso` feature is NOT in the default feature set. So a plain `cargo test --workspace` never compiles src/persistence/turso_backend.rs at all: the `impl WriteTxn for TursoBackend` block is stripped before type-checking. Adding a new required method to the trait therefore breaks ONLY the feature-gated impl, and E0046 stays invisible under the default command. Rust's default-feature compilation is not a subset check on feature-gated code paths: `cfg`-stripped modules are not compiled, so no trait-conformance error can fire for them.

FIX (two parts):
1. Implement the new trait method on EVERY impl, including the feature-gated one. In this case `append_messages_batch` was added to the SqliteWriteTxn impl (correctly) but not to `impl WriteTxn for TursoBackend`, so gather the sibling impls by grepping `impl <Trait> for` rather than trusting the compiler to list them — under default features the compiler cannot tell you they are missing.
2. Adopt the full-feature command as the configured gate: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` (or at minimum `cargo build --workspace --all-features`). `--all-features` is what makes E0046 on gated impls fire locally instead of in CI.

VERIFICATION (all run in the repo, in this order):
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` -> exit 0 (was exit 101 with E0046).
- `cargo build --workspace --all-features` -> exit 0.
- `cargo test --workspace` -> exit 0, every target `test result: ok`, including the two new regression tests for the added method.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` -> exit 0 (the FIRST attempt at this change also failed CI on a Format leg: hand-written Rust that compiles and passes tests can still fail `cargo fmt --check`; always run the formatter before pushing).
- CI after push: 3/3 legs success (format, lint, test) on the fix commit; the pre-fix commit's run shows conclusion=failure on the Format leg.

TRAP TO REMEMBER: a green `cargo test --workspace` is NOT evidence that a trait addition is complete when any impl is `cfg`-gated. A green default-feature build plus a red `--all-features` build is the signature of exactly this class. Also note the reverse hazard: `cargo test --workspace` (default features) can be green while `cargo test --workspace --all-features` exercises a DIFFERENT set of impls, so any acceptance criterion phrased as 'the repo builds' must name the feature set explicitly.

RELATED BUT DISTINCT mechanism (do not confuse): Cargo feature UNIFICATION (E0599 / `serialize_struct` not found) where resolver 1 leaks a dep's features across workspace members and `resolver = "2"` plus feature forwarding is the fix. That class is about a dependency's features being unified; THIS class is about a local `impl Trait for T` block being cfg-stripped out of the compilation unit entirely.
